content: The test image shows a plant stem near the soil line with white cottony mycelial growth and dark round sclerotia embedded in the mycelium. This is characteristic of either Southern Blight or Sclerotinia Timber Rot. Let me view a reference image.

The reference image for Southern Blight shows whole-plant wilt at field scale. My test image shows a close-up of a stem near soil level with white cottony mycelium and dark, round sclerotia — the hallmark signature of Sclerotium rolfsii (Southern Blight).

Key features in the test image:
- **Affected part**: Stem at/near soil line
- **White cottony mycelium**: Fluffy, dense white fungal growth wrapping the stem
- **Dark round sclerotia**: Small, black/dark-brown spherical bodies embedded in the mycelium — the diagnostic feature of S. rolfsii
- **Stem decay**: Underlying tissue is rotted and brown

This matches Southern Blight closely. Sclerotinia Timber Rot would produce larger, rat-dropping-shaped sclerotia (typically inside the stem), not the small round mustard-seed sclerotia seen here.
